I realized that selling all my buildings first would raise my liquidation to roughly $2485. That is well above the Boardwalk threshold, so even a fully built-up green monopoly would not kill me.

No mutually beneficial trade exists. The only way to make Boardwalk lethal is to raise red rents so any red hit drops them below the kill line, while keeping enough cash to survive my own trip around the board.

I am simulating how the Boardwalk survival margin changes as I pay rent. The expected rent from this roll is only about $25, so building both reds is safe. I am now weighing whether to build just Indiana instead, since it is hit more often from this position and would leave more cash for the income tax and repairs.

The Kentucky upgrade is speculative for later. One house on Indiana is the sharper play because of cash safety. I will lap back to Med and Baltic in roughly six turns. They have six turns to reach Boardwalk or Park Place before I return.

In either case, the brown threat disappears even if they survive.

I will build both reds to two houses. The brown threat only disappears once they are forced to liquidate buildings, which is still many turns away. I can rebuild cash from their rent payments and GO money while waiting.

The Boardwalk hotel no longer threatens bankruptcy, and I have already passed it. The prior cash-cushion concern is resolved, so building both reds to two houses is now the correct play. I am also confirming the standard house cost of $150 and the Indiana Avenue rent table.

I will build the houses now and end my turn on the following decision. I will not unmortgage or trade. I will send a short neutral message without revealing the kill setup.

A mortgaged railroad is worth only about fifty to one hundred dollars in expected landings, so the opponent will not pay one hundred thirty-four dollars for it. Even a one-hundred-dollar offer would leave them barely above the Boardwalk death line, and accepting it would shrink the gap to thirty-three dollars. At that point, Kentucky Avenue at ninety dollars would close the gap entirely, making the trade unviable.

I will build both reds to two houses. The public message will be "Reds needed a touch-up."

I also checked whether Illinois Avenue at three houses could kill the opponent through the Park Place landing. Three houses there cost $750, leaving them with $1383 after rent. That is still above the $1500 survival margin, so it would not be lethal.

Three houses on Illinois Avenue would leave only twenty dollars cash, so any rent payment would force a sale before the opponent circles. That makes the upgrade unstable and too risky. I will keep two houses on every red property instead.
